quarto generate project website:

``` bash
quarto create project Website
```

initialize git repository:

``` bash
git init
```

then config `_quarto.yml` to set up the website.

We can have `renv` to manage R packages:

``` bash
renv::init()
```

Then add `renv` to `.gitignore`:

``` bash
echo "renv/library" >> .gitignore
echo "renv/staging" >> .gitignore
echo "renv/python" >> .gitignore
echo "renv/settings.dcf" >> .gitignore
echo "renv/activate.R" >> .gitignore
echo "renv.lock" >> .gitignore
echo ".Rprofile" >> .gitignore
echo ".Rhistory" >> .gitignore
echo ".RData" >> .gitignore
echo ".Rproj.user" >> .gitignore
echo ".Rproj" >> .gitignore
echo ".DS_Store" >> .gitignore
```

Then commit the changes:

``` bash
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit"
```

If i finished and wanted to update `renv`:

``` r
renv::snapshot()
renv::status()
```

I i downloaded new repo and wanted to restore `renv`:

``` r
renv::restore()
renv::status()
```

Go to GitHub to create a new repository, then copy the commands to push local repo to GitHub.

``` bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/vahdatjavad/bash.git   
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

Then I can use GitHub to host the website.

``` bash
git remote add origin
git branch -M main
git push -u origin main
```

Then I can go to GitHub repository setting to enable GitHub pages.

for rendering the website:

``` bash
quarto render --output-dir docs
```

Then commit and push to GitHub:

``` bash
git add .
git commit -m "Render website"
git push
```

Then I can go to GitHub repository setting to enable GitHub pages.
